name: Sidney

seo.title: Landscaping in Sidney, BC — Strata Grounds & Trees | RNC
seo.description: Strata grounds care, hedge and tree work, irrigation and planting for Sidney condos, homes and Beacon Avenue frontages, with the Town's tree permits.

h1: Landscaping and garden care in Sidney
summary: Sidney is compact: condo and apartment stratas, seniors' residences and small lots around Beacon Avenue and Roberts Bay. The Town's 2025 flood mapping treats the first 30 m from the shoreline as the land most exposed to wave run-up and spray, which shapes what grows on waterfront strata grounds.

Wood burning is not allowed anywhere in the Town, so prunings go to curbside yard-waste collection or are hauled, and the curbside service will not take blackberry or any invasive plant. The Tree Preservation Bylaw protects Garry oak, arbutus and Pacific dogwood from 3 cm across, and Douglas-fir and western redcedar from 1.2 m tall.

localRules.text: Sidney's Tree Preservation Bylaw 2138 protects listed native species, replacement trees, trees required by a development permit, trees in environmental development permit areas, Town trees and any tree over 60 cm in diameter.
localRules.sourceTitle: Tree Preservation Bylaw - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: Any tree having a diameter greater than 60 cm

localRules.text: Under Bylaw 2138, Douglas-fir, bigleaf maple, grand fir and western redcedar are protected once they are 1.2 m tall. Arbutus, cascara, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood, seaside juniper, shore pine and western yew are protected from 3 cm in diameter, measured 1.4 m above the ground.
localRules.sourceTitle: Tree Preservation Bylaw 2138 (consolidated) - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: Western Redcedar (Thuja plicata) trees with a height of 1.2 metres or more, and Arbutus (Arbutus menziesii), Cascara (Rhamnus purshiana), Garry Oak (Quercus garryana)

localRules.text: Without a permit, Sidney allows up to 20% of a protected tree's crown to be pruned in a season, to ISA or ASCA standards, for the tree's health. Cutting any branch, stem or root over 5 cm in diameter (over 2.5 cm for arbutus, Pacific dogwood and Garry oak) needs a Tree Permit, and fill, materials or structures may not go inside a protected tree's drip line.
localRules.sourceTitle: Tree Preservation Bylaw 2138 (consolidated) - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: up to 20% of Crown of a Protected Tree during a season for the purpose of maintaining or improving the health of the Tree.

localRules.text: On private land, removing, extensively pruning or topping a protected tree may need a Tree Removal Permit. The Town asks owners to call the Parks Department (250-656-1034) to talk to Sidney's arborist before starting.
localRules.sourceTitle: Tree Preservation Bylaw - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: To remove, extensively prune, or top an existing tree located on private property, you may require a Tree Removal Permit.

localRules.text: Sidney's tree permit application covers pruning and removal of protected trees. Every protected tree removed needs replacement trees and a refundable per-tree deposit, returned if the new trees are healthy after two years; if they are not planted on site, the Town plants them on Town land and charges a per-tree fee in lieu.
localRules.excerpt: This deposit will be returned if the trees are healthy after 2 years, upon approval by the Town Arborist.

localRules.text: Sidney's tree permit application requires that tree removal and pruning be done by a certified arborist hired by the applicant.
localRules.excerpt: Tree removal and pruning must be done by a certified arborist contracted by the applicant.

localRules.text: Properties in Sidney's Environmentally Sensitive Area development permit areas, which take in creeks, shorelines and upland forest, need an approved development permit before any construction or landscaping that significantly affects the land or water.
localRules.sourceTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: Properties within an Environmentally Sensitive Area DPA require an approved Development Permit prior to any construction or landscaping that has a significant impact on the land or water.

localRules.text: In Sidney's environmentally sensitive areas, gardening and yard maintenance within an existing landscaped area is among the common exempt activities. Changes to landscaping that alter the land can need a development permit, so the Town suggests talking to staff early.
localRules.sourceTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: gardening and yard maintenance within an existing landscaped area

localRules.text: Sidney's marine-shoreline environmentally sensitive area takes in already-developed waterfront lots, many with older concrete seawalls. When those lots are rebuilt, the guidelines look to protect or restore natural shoreline and vegetation, keep building back from the high-water mark, or use naturalized approaches such as Green Shores.
localRules.sourceTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: protect or restore natural shoreline and vegetation, avoid construction that is too close to the high water mark, or incorporate naturalized solutions, such as GreenShores

localRules.text: Under Sidney's Boulevard Maintenance Bylaw 1738 (2002), owners keep the boulevard next to their property neat and tidy and the grass cut. The Town can deem a boulevard unsightly or a hazard, direct the owner in writing to maintain it, and if the owner does not, do the work at the owner's expense.
localRules.excerpt: All owners of real property shall maintain the boulevard in a neat and tidy condition and shall keep the grass cut on all boulevards that abut a street

localRules.text: Wood burning is not allowed in Sidney. Residential waste, construction-site, demolition, land-clearing and beach fires are prohibited; propane and charcoal fire pits are permitted.
localRules.excerpt: Wood burning within the Town of Sidney is not permitted.

localRules.text: Sidney's curbside yard-waste collection will not take morning glory, blackberry, wild mustard, ox-eye daisy, wild carrot, couch grass, poison hemlock or any invasive plant species, so invasive clearings need separate disposal.
localRules.sourceTitle: Yard & Garden Waste - Town of Sidney
localRules.excerpt: Morning glory, blackberry, wild mustard, ox-eye daisy, wild carrot, couch grass, poison hemlock, and all invasive plant species are unacceptable.

conditions.text: Reay Creek and Mermaid Creek provide fish habitat and help filter stormwater, so lots next to them may also fall under the Province's riparian rules.
conditions.sourceTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas - Town of Sidney
conditions.excerpt: properties around Mermaid Creek and Reay Creek may be subject to the Province’s Riparian Areas Protection Regulation.

conditions.text: Sidney's 2025 flood mapping treats the first 30 m inland from the shoreline as a wave effect zone, the land most exposed to wave run-up and spray. Plants and features there face salt and storm exposure. The mapped flood construction levels are not yet regulatory; the Town's interim policy still applies.
conditions.sourceTitle: Sea Level Rise - Town of Sidney
conditions.excerpt: Land within 30 meters of the shoreline is most exposed to wave run-up and spray.

conditions.text: Sidney's contractor collects yard and garden waste at the curb twice a month. Each household may set out up to three lidless rigid cans or three kraft-paper yard bags of up to 80 L and 20 kg each, and branches must be under 3 inches in diameter, in bundles up to 3 ft long. There is no yard-waste pickup for commercial units.
conditions.sourceTitle: Yard & Garden Waste - Town of Sidney
conditions.excerpt: Households may put out up to three rigid garbage cans without lids or three compostable craft paper yard waste bags, with a maximum volume of 80L and 20kg (44lbs) each.

conditions.text: Sidney gets its water from the CRD system fed by Sooke Lake, and the Town notes that the CRD's Stage 1 watering schedule applies every year from May 1 to September 30.
conditions.excerpt: The Town receives water from the Capital Regional District (CRD) trunk distribution system from Sooke Lake.

conditions.text: Sidney has a Community Wildfire Resiliency Plan (2024) supporting its FireSmart program, and the Fire Department points residents to the FireSmart BC Landscaping Guide.
conditions.excerpt: The Town of Sidney has developed a Community Wildfire Resiliency Plan (CWRP) for Sidney to guide the Town’s efforts to prevent and respond to potential wildfires.

proof.text: Reduced a Roberts Bay strata's boundary hedge over two seasons, staying under the Town's 20% crown limit on the protected shore pine at one end of the row.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Sidney owners keep the boulevard next to their property neat and the grass cut, so strata visits include that frontage.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: Gardening in an existing landscaped area is exempt inside Sidney's environmentally sensitive areas, but changing the land itself can need a development permit.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: The Town draws its water through the CRD system from Sooke Lake, and it reminds residents that Stage 1 lawn days run from May through September.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Without a permit, Sidney allows up to 20% of a protected tree's crown to be pruned in a season, and the Town's permit form requires a certified arborist for permitted work.
